knowledge_units.context_summary: The paper investigates the local existence, finite-time blow-up, and global existence of solutions for a system of nonlocal nonlinear coupled wave equations. The model generalizes one-dimensional nonlocal elasticity and includes coupled Boussinesq-type equations as special cases. The authors establish results under conditions where kernel functions have nonnegative Fourier transforms with specific decay rates.

It defines the maximal time of existence and provides a criterion for global existence based on the boundedness of the L-infinity norm. The proof relies on converting the PDE to an ODE system and demonstrating the Lipschitz continuity of the nonlinear terms.

knowledge_units.context_summary: The text establishes conditions for finite-time blow-up when initial energy is positive, specifically requiring the square of the initial momentum inner product to be less than the product of initial energy and position norm. It then proves global existence for solutions under two kernel classes: sufficiently smooth kernels with decay rate greater than 3, and mildly singular kernels with a jump in the first derivative.
